question_set.question: Use trace_node with node_name equal to AAA Orig and use trace_node with node_name equal to Junk Orig in order to know How do the credit migration patterns differ between high-quality (AAA/AA) and lower-quality (BBB/Junk) loans over the three-year period?

answer.value: High-quality loans (AAA/AA) show strong rating stability with over 80% retaining their rating or improving, and minimal default risk (<1% cumulative). Lower-quality loans (BBB/Junk) exhibit significant downgrade pressure with 30-50% migrating to worse ratings and substantial default rates (27% for Junk in Y1 alone). The migration patterns reveal that BBB and Junk loans are the primary sources of default, while AAA/AA loans act as safe anchors in the portfolio.

key_insights: AAA loans have 84% retention rate in Y1
AAA loans have zero direct default risk
Junk loans have 27% default rate in Y1 alone
Lower-quality loans show significant downgrade pressure

reasoning_trace.rationale: Trace the outflow patterns of AAA Orig to understand high-quality loan migration
Trace the outflow patterns of Junk Orig to understand lower-quality loan migration
